reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every real inner-product space E,every real kappa>=1 and every z=(x,p) in E x E,let Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2. Then
  ||x||^2+||p||^2 <= 6 Q_kappa(x,p).
The left-hand energy is the coordinate sum of squared E norms,not the square of the default maximum product norm. The statement gives this one global pointwise inequality without requiring completeness,finite-dimensionality or a measure.
objects: Real inner-product E;real kappa>=1;arbitrary phase vector z;coordinate-sum ordinary energy and explicit quadratic energy Q_kappa.
domains: E is a real inner-product space;kappa in R;z=(x,p) in E x E. Both energies and the inequality are real-valued. No extra space or measure structure is imposed.
quantifiers: For every E,kappa with kappa>=1,and every z in E x E,the displayed inequality holds. No existential witness or integration variable appears.
assumptions: kappa>=1 and the real-inner-product/norm structure. Q_kappa has its explicit definition from the approved context. No completeness,dimension,moment or probability assumption is present.
conclusion: The coordinate-sum energy ||x||^2+||p||^2 is <=6Q_kappa(x,p),for every phase vector.
scopes: One direction of pointwise energy comparison only. The ordinary energy means the explicit sum,not a default product norm. No reverse comparison,transport theorem or nonlinear update statement is included. No ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: Exact universal comparison factor is 6,uniform in kappa>=1 and phase vector. Q has position coefficient 1/(2kappa)+1/2,cross coefficient 1,momentum coefficient 1. No dimension or unspecified constant appears.
